text:
Maya S.: FYI, ACME (tenant id: acme-778) opened a support ticket — p99 latency spike from ~120ms -> ~3s across their chat endpoints starting at 08:05 PST. Customer says responses started to stall and sometimes return 500s. We see GPU memory pressure and occasional OOM recoveries on nodes handling their shards.

Arjun K.: thanks, can you paste the dashboard link and a short repro (curl) we can run? any recent deploys?

Maya S.: Dashboard: https://rbw-infer.internal/acme/tenants/acme-778/perf (private). No full infra deploys recorded at 07:50-08:10, but a model catalog refresh + new quantized variant was promoted at 07:58 for many tenants. Customer traffic pattern: long-running chat sessions with big contexts (avg tokens per request up ~4x). Repro (sanitized):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-v2-q4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<~15k tokens context>"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat
```

Maya S.: quick logs from one affected runtime pod: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:06:12Z] runtime: kv-cache bytes=1.9GB entries=36412
[2026-03-17T08:06:12Z] runtime WARN: gpu-mem-high: used=14.7GB total=16GB fragmentation=22%
[2026-03-17T08:06:13Z] allocator: triggered slab-split, reclaimed=0MB
[2026-03-17T08:06:14Z] runtime ERROR: OOM-recover: drop-kv-entries=1024
```

Sam P.: kv-cache at 1.9GB for a single tenant is huge. Looks like a leak or unbounded per-tenant cache. Do we enforce per-tenant kv caps currently?

Lena R.: not strictly — we have cluster-wide heuristics and LRU, but long-lived sessions with pinned prefixes can keep entries alive. The new q4 variant increases per-token decode concurrency which increases KV working set.

Arjun K.: Can we triage quickly: 1) capture pmap/nvidia-smi for the pod; 2) run `curl /debug/kv-stats`; 3) temporarily limit this tenant's model to smaller variant / lower concurrency or route to dedicated pool.

Maya S.: collecting outputs now. nvtop shows one tensor consuming ~6.4GB pinned + multiple small fragments. `curl /debug/kv-stats` returns: 
```
tenant: acme-778
kv_total_bytes: 1973242368
kv_entries: 36412
kv_evictions: 12 (last 5m)
cache_hit: 0.82
longest_entry_seconds: 86400
```

Maya S.: applied temporary rate-limit for acme-778 (50% of normal concurrency) via the console routing layer at 08:12 — customer still seeing some p99s but fewer OOM logs.

Sam P.: good. Short-term mitigations we should try now (in priority):
- enable per-tenant KV soft-cap: set RW_KV_MAX_BYTES=200MB for the tenant via runtime env override
- lower per-request decode concurrency: set DECODER_MAX_THREADS=8 for the pod handling that shard
- route acme-778 to fallback model `gpt-lite-v1-q4a` (smaller kv footprint)
- if pressure persists, restart the affected pod with gpu-defrag mode enabled (`--gpu-defrag=true`)

Lena R.: I'll push the env override and a rolling restart for the two hot pods. Also raise allocator tuning: GPU_ALLOC_SLICE_BYTES=65536 (smaller slice to reduce external fragmentation) and set KV_EVICT_BATCH=4096 for faster eviction under pressure.

Maya S.: commands you're running?

Lena R.: running internal admin API: 
```
# set per-tenant cap
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.internal/runtime/tenants/acme-778/config \
  -d '{"RW_KV_MAX_BYTES":"209715200"}'

# update pod env (k8s rollout)
kubectl set env deployment/inference-runtime RUNTIME_FLAGS="--gpu-defrag=true --gpu-alloc-slice=65536 --kv-evict-batch=4096" -n runtime
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n runtime
```

Arjun K.: note: the rollout will briefly reduce capacity; prefer targeted restart of the two pods serving acme-778 first (use label selector). Also schedule a canary to validate that eviction doesn't regress quality.

Maya S.: applied tenant cap at 08:18. Doing targeted restart of pods runtime-87 and runtime-91 now. Will keep customer updated.

deploy-bot: deployment/inference-runtime restarted (pods: runtime-87, runtime-91) — 08:21:05

Maya S.: post-restart metrics (08:28): p99 dropped to 240ms, kv_total_bytes for acme-778 down to 186MB, evictions spiked then leveled. No further OOM logs. Customer reports much improved responsiveness.

Sam P.: looks like root cause = combination of: new q4 variant increasing per-request KV usage + tenant long contexts + no strict per-tenant cap -> KV growth -> GPU fragmentation -> OOM-recover slow paths. Fixes: enforce per-tenant caps, smaller alloc slice, kv-evict batch tuning, optional defrag on restart.

Arjun K.: follow-ups:
- add an alert for per-tenant kv bytes > 400MB sustained (prod runbook)
- add a safe fallback policy for when allocator fragmentation >20% (auto-route to smaller model)
- update docs for support playbook (steps we did + commands)

Maya S.: I'll file a postmortem ticket and notify ACME that we've implemented the cap and rolled a focused fix. Will include repro steps and recommended customer guidance: avoid extremely long pinned prefixes or switch to streaming chunks.

Lena R.: creating infra PR to make per-tenant RW_KV_MAX_BYTES configurable via routing rules and to default GPU_ALLOC_SLICE_BYTES=65536 for heavy models.

Maya S.: thanks all — closing thread after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
